issues.legal_issue: The statutory time limit for making an acquisition declaration does not also limit the time for publishing it.
material_facts: An initial acquisition notification was published, and the declaration was formally made within the applicable one-year period following that publication.
The declaration was published in the Official Gazette after that one-year period.
The landowner challenged the declaration as time-barred because its publication occurred after the period expired.
issues.conclusion: The declaration was valid because it was made within the prescribed period; its later publication did not make it time-barred.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 6(1), including its first proviso, the prescribed period governs when the declaration must be made. Section 6(2) requires publication of the declaration but sets no time limit for that publication; publication is evidence of the declaration, whose legal effect as conclusive evidence is addressed by Section 6(3). The Court followed the binding four-judge decision in Khadim Hussain v. State of U.P. and held that the contrary observations in other cited cases did not displace it.

predicates.land_acquisition_proceeding: The proceeding concerns a government's acquisition of land for a public purpose or another permitted acquisition purpose.
predicates.declaration_made_within_applicable_time_: The competent authority formally made the acquisition declaration within the time allowed after publication of the initial acquisition notification.
predicates.declaration_published_after_that_limit: The declaration was published after the time allowed for formally making it had expired.

issues.definition: When an acquisition proceeding involves a declaration made within the applicable time limit but published after it, the later publication does not make the declaration invalid.
